### iliad-114 (17.582–672)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε μέγας Τελαμώνιος Αἴας (17.628, whole-line speech introduction) | "And among them of speeches made-beginning great Telamonian Ajax:" | "Great Telamonian Ajax was the first to speak among them:" | "addressed" (reserved for προσέφη), "Ajax son of Telamon"; follows the table's τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε Ποσειδάων ἐνοσίχθων (7.445) and "great Telamonian Ajax" |
| τῷ μιν ἐεισάμενος προσέφη ἑκάεργος Ἀπόλλων (17.585) | "Having made himself like to that man, addressed him far-working Apollo:" | "Making himself like that man, Apollo, who works from afar, said to him:" | "the far-shooter"; ἑκάεργος "far-working" (15.243), with the shape of the published τῷ μιν ἐεισάμενος … Διὸς υἱὸς Ἀπόλλων (iliad-106, -111) |
| οἷον δὴ Μενέλαον ὑπέτρεσας (17.587) | "Such a Menelaus you took fright at" | "You took fright at such a man as Menelaus" | "feared", "shrank from", "were afraid of" (ταρβέω keeps "terrified", 17.586, as the table’s ταρβήσας χαλκόν 6.469); τρέω "take fright", ὑπο- as "at, before" |
| μαλθακὸς αἰχμητής (17.588) | "a soft spearman" | "a soft spearman" | "weak", "cowardly", "gentle"; μαλθακός "soft", αἰχμητής "spearman" |
| πιστὸν ἑταῖρον (17.589) | "trusty companion" | "trusty companion" | "faithful" (the Odyssey’s πιστὸς ἑταῖρος, 15.539; the Iliad’s own row at 15.331 has "trusty"), "loyal", "true"; follows the table’s πιστὸν ἑταῖρον (15.331) |
| ὣς φάτο, τὸν δ’ ἄχεος νεφέλη ἐκάλυψε μέλαινα (17.591; = Odyssey 24.315, odyssey-117) | "So he spoke, and him a cloud of grief covered, dark" | "So he spoke, and a dark cloud of grief covered Hector" | the Odyssey's `i` ("covered the old man") with the man named for the Iliad context; the Odyssey's `l` kept unchanged |
| ἐπιλίγδην (ἄκρον ἐπιλίγδην, 17.599) | "at the top, grazingly" | "at the top, with a grazing blow" (+ note: rare word, sense taken from γράψεν) | "lightly", "on the surface", "in passing" (each decides the rare word's sense differently) |
| γράψεν δέ οἱ ὀστέον ἄχρις (17.599) | "scratched for him, right to the bone" | "scratched him right to the bone" (+ note: ἄχρις after ὀστέον, grammar not quite clear) | "scraped the bone clean", "scratched the bone utterly" (each makes ὀστέον the object); γράφω "scratch" |
| καυλός (ἐν καυλῷ δ’ ἐάγη δολιχὸν δόρυ, 17.607) | "At the stem broke the long spear" | "The long spear broke at the stem" (+ note: exact place not certain) | "at the socket", "at the shaft", "at the tang" (each fixes the part); καυλός "stem" |
| ὀπάων · ἡνίοχος (Μηριόναο ὀπάονά θ’ ἡνίοχόν τε, 17.610) | "follower and charioteer" | "follower and charioteer" | "attendant" (reserved for θεράπων, 13.246), "squire", "driver"; follows the table’s ὀπάων "follower" (7.165) and ἡνίοχος "charioteer" (5.231) |
| ἐγγυάλιξεν (καί κε Τρωσὶ μέγα κράτος ἐγγυάλιξεν, 17.613) | "to the Trojans great strength he would have put into their hands" | "Hector would have put great strength into the hands of the Trojans" (+ note: subject not stated; Hector on the reading of the condition) | "victory", "glory" (reserved for κῦδος); as the table's ἐγγυάλιξε (11.753); the subject is named in `i` only |
| φάος ἦλθεν (17.615) | "light came" | "the light of safety came" (+ note: φάος stands for rescue) | "deliverance came", "daylight came", "he saw the light"; the table's νηλεὲς ἦμαρ "pitiless day" with ἀμύνω "ward off" |
| πρυμνὸν δόρυ (ἐκ δ’ ἄρ’ ὀδόντας ὦσε δόρυ πρυμνόν, 17.618) | "pushed the spear, hindmost" | "the spear drove the teeth out, going in all the way" (+ note: sense not certain) | "to the base", "by the butt", "at the root" (each fixes an uncertain word) |
| ἡνία (κατὰ δ’ ἡνία χεῦεν ἔραζε, 17.619) | "the reins he poured down to the ground" | "spilled the reins to the ground" | "dropped", "let fall"; χέω "pour" (as ἠέρα … ἔχευεν, 8.50), κατά in tmesis "down" |
| ἵμασεν καλλίτριχας ἵππους (17.624) | "lashed the fair-maned horses" | "lashed his fair-maned horses on" | "whipped" (reserved for μαστίζω; Meriones' μάστιε is "Whip"); follows ἱμάσσω "lashed" (5.380) |
| δέος ἔμπεσε θυμῷ (17.625) | "fear fell upon his heart" | "fear had fallen upon his heart" | "terror", "dread" (Δεῖμος); δέος "fear" (4.421) |
| οὐδ’ ἔλαθ’ … Ζεύς (17.626) | "And did not escape … Zeus" | "Zeus did not escape the notice of …" | "Ajax and Menelaus did not fail to see", "was not hidden from"; λανθάνω "escape notice of" |
| ἑτεραλκέα νίκην (17.627, without μάχης) | "a victory, other-strengthening" | "a victory that turns the fight to the other side" | the table's ἑτεραλκέα νίκην (7.26, "a victory in battle, other-strengthening"); "in battle" is left out only because the Greek here has no μάχης |
| ἅπτεται (βέλε’ ἅπτεται, 17.631) | "the shafts reach their mark" | "the shafts of all of them hit home" | "touch", "lay hold" in `i`; "missiles" (the Odyssey’s alternative, turned down by the table’s βέλος "shaft", 4.542); ἅπτω "fasten on" |
| ἰθύνει (Ζεὺς δ’ ἔμπης πάντ’ ἰθύνει, 17.632) | "guides all things straight" | "guides everything straight" | "directs", "steers", "aims"; follows ἴθυνεν "guided straight" (5.290) |
| αὔτως (ἡμῖν δ’ αὔτως πᾶσιν ἐτώσια πίπτει, 17.633) | "just so" | "simply" (with ἐτώσια "in vain") | "to no purpose" and "for nothing" are the table's `i` for other uses; ἐτώσια takes "in vain" |
| μῆτιν ἀρίστην (φραζώμεθα μῆτιν ἀρίστην, 17.634) | "plan the best cunning" | "plan the best stroke of cunning" | "devise" (reserved for συμφράσσατο, 1.537), "plan" as the noun (reserved for βουλή; μῆτις is "cunning", 2.169, 10.497), "the best way"; φράζομαι "plan" (1.554) |
| ἀάπτους (χεῖρας ἀάπτους, 17.638) | "untouchable" | "irresistible" (+ note: meaning not known) | the table's ἀάπτους (11.502, 13.318), unchanged |
| σχήσεσθ’ … πεσέεσθαι (17.639) | "will we hold back … but in the black ships will fall" | "we shall no longer hold back … but shall fall at the black ships" | the published iliad-054 wording "upon the black ships" (the Trojans attacking); here the Achaeans fall at the ships, so "upon" is dropped; σχήσεσθαι "hold back" |
| ἀκηχέδατ’ (17.637) | "are grieved" | "are grieved" | "are troubled", "mourn"; old perfect from the root of ἄχος "grief" |
| λυγρῆς ἀγγελίης (17.642) | "the grievous news" | "the grievous news" | "message" (withdrawn by the table), "bitter", "baneful" (reserved for other words); λυγρός "grievous" (5.156), ἀγγελίη "news" (2.787) |
| ἠέρα … ὀμίχλην (17.649) | "the mist … the fog" | "the mist … the fog" | "mist … mist" (both are "mist" in the table: ἠήρ 8.50, ὀμίχλη 1.359); the two words in one line are told apart: ἠήρ "mist", ὀμίχλη "fog" |
| ἐπὶ πᾶσα φαάνθη (μάχη δ’ ἐπὶ πᾶσα φαάνθη, 17.650) | "the whole battle came into view" | "the whole battle came into view" | "shone", "was lit up" (ἐπέλαμψε is "shone"); φαίνω "show" |
| ὥς τίς τε λέων ἀπὸ μεσσαύλοιο (17.657) | "like some lion from the farmyard" | "like a lion going away from the farmyard" | "stall", "steading", "cattle-pen"; follows iliad-069's "the cattle’s farmyard" (11.548) |
| ἐρεθίζων (κύνας τ’ ἄνδρας τ’ ἐρεθίζων, 17.658) | "provoking" | "provoking" | "goading", "rousing", "harrying"; ἐρεθίζω "provoke" |
| ἠῶθεν δ’ ἀπονόσφιν ἔβη τετιηότι θυμῷ (17.664) | "and at dawn away, apart, he went with grieved heart" | "and at dawn he goes off, away, grieved at heart" | the published 11.555 wording, unchanged (the edition prints ἀπὸ νόσφιν as two words there, ἀπονόσφιν as one here) |
| ἀργαλέου πρὸ φόβοιο (17.667) | "before grievous flight" | "in the face of grievous flight" | "terrible", "cruel", "hard"; ἀργαλέος "grievous" (11.812), φόβος "flight" |
| ἐπέτελλεν (πολλὰ δὲ Μηριόνῃ … ἐπέτελλεν, 17.668) | "he laid charge" | "he laid many charges on" | "ordered", "commanded"; follows ἐπέτελλεν "laid his charge" (iliad-070) |
| ἐνηείης (17.670; ἐνηής "kindly") | "kindness" | "kindness" | "gentleness" (kept for μείλιχος, 17.671), "mildness", "goodness"; rare noun |
| δειλοῖο (Πατροκλῆος δειλοῖο, 17.670) | "miserable" | "miserable" | "poor", "wretched" (reserved for δύστηνος); follows the table's δειλός "miserable" |
| μείλιχος εἶναι (17.671) | "gentle" | "gentle" | "kind" (ἐνηείη), "sweet", "mild"; μείλιχος "gentle", as μειλίχιος |
| Names (17.582–672) | Phaenops · Asius · Abydus · Podes · Eetion · Ida · Peneleos · Polydamas · Leitus · Alectryon · Idomeneus · Deucalion · Meriones · Coeranus · Lyctus · Antilochus · Nestor · Menelaus · Achilles · Patroclus · Ajaxes (plural) | same, "son of …" for patronymics in `i` | the familiar Latinised forms, as for the other names in the table |

Reused unchanged (no new row): the published lines at 17.651 (iliad-110, whole unit verbatim), 17.656 (iliad-110, whole unit verbatim), 17.659–660a (iliad-069, whole unit verbatim), 17.660b–661a (iliad-069, whole unit verbatim), 17.661b–663 (iliad-069, wording verbatim; the Greek has a comma after χειρῶν that the published unit lacks), 17.648 (iliad-048, the line only, `l` and `i` as published), 17.592 (iliad-026, `l` wording kept for the line), 17.639 (see the row above).
